title: AI Search Finds 546 Possible Exoplanets Missing From NASA TESS List
summary:
Astronomical data processed by independent analysts has revealed orbital patterns suggesting the presence of distant planetary bodies. A wide scale scan of 4 million stars within the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) dataset identified 546 possible exoplanets, none of which are currently listed in official NASA catalogs, according to a researcher who built upon a method developed by Pavel Rabtsevich.

The discovery method utilizes Claude Code along with Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 AI models to analyze stellar light curves. Rabtsevich previously identified a candidate 116 light-years away that is about 1.4 times the size of Earth and orbits its star every 3.18 days. NASA has approved telescope time for its TESS mission to verify Rabtsevich's findings from Oct 31 to Nov 26.

selectedTweets.bestBit: TESS will check it again from Oct 31 to Nov 26
selectedTweets.text:
This post is absolutely going viral on Reddit 

An independent researcher used Claude Code to find a possible new planet. It had been sitting in NASA's TESS data since 2018, and he could find no earlier report of it.

Claude Code with Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.1 did most of the work: parsing the light curves, writing the transit search, fitting transits, checking nearby stars and secondary eclipses. He set the questions and the pass/fail rules.

The star is about 116 light-years away. Every 3.18 days it dims by about 0.05% for two hours, which fits a planet about 1.4 times the size of Earth. It is still a candidate, and TESS will check it again from Oct 31 to Nov 26.
